newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel - short-term forex moves no cause for concern.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - short-term forex moves no cause for concern.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that short term fluctuations on foreign exchange markets were no cause for concern and there was no reason to doubt the euro's stability.
Waigel also said that the current strength of sterling and the dollar reflected the strength of the British and U.S. economies.
"Short term currency fluctuations are no grounds for worry," Waigel said, repeating an earlier message from Bonn relayed by a government spokesman.
Waigel, addressing a banking audience, said there were always "fluctuations and speculative exaggerations" between major currencies.
Markets had no justification for doubting the stability of the euro, Waigel said.
"Nothing is being softened or interpreted in a lax manner here," he said.
Germany would continue to insist on strict adherence to the Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria, Waigel said.
The German government earlier signalled that it wanted to play down the recent fall in the mark's value against the pound sterling and the dollar.
In words later labelled by economists as too weak to halt the mark's decline, a spokesman said there was no reason to dramatise recent developments on foreign exchange markets
